# Conformance vector schema

A vector is one JSON file asserting a fact from
[`docs/02-go-rules-spec.md`](../docs/02-go-rules-spec.md). The Swift engine
(`sente-ios/Packages/GoKit`) and the Go engine (`sente-server/internal/rules`)
both run every file in `vectors/`; either suite failing means the engines have
drifted apart ([ADR-002](../docs/03-solution-design.md#adr-002--nơi-đặt-engine-luật-cờ)).

**Vectors are authored by hand.** A vector generated by the engine it tests
proves nothing. Every expectation below was derived from the specification, not
from a program's output.

## Coordinates

Display coordinates throughout: column letters `A`–`T` with **I omitted**, rows
numbered **from the bottom**. `d4` is the lower-left star point on 19×19, `q16`
the upper-right one. Case-insensitive.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique; matches the filename |
| `description` | string | What the vector pins down, and why it matters |
| `rules` | `japanese` \| `chinese` | Default `japanese` |
| `board_size` | 9 \| 13 \| 19 | Default 19 |
| `komi` | number | Default: 6.5 Japanese, 7.5 Chinese, 0.5 with handicap |
| `handicap` | 0, or 2–9 | Non-zero places stones and makes White move first |
| `setup` | `{black: [], white: []}` | Starting stones; ignored when `handicap` > 0 |
| `to_play` | `black` \| `white` | Default `black` |
| `captures` | `{black: n, white: n}` | Prisoners already held before the vector runs |
| `moves` | `["B:e5", "W:pass"]` | Played before the assertion; each must be legal |
| `move` | coordinate \| `pass` \| `resign` | The move under test |
| `move_by` | `black` \| `white` | Who attempts `move`; defaults to whoever is to play |
| `dead_stones` | `["b1"]` | Stones agreed dead, for scoring assertions |
| `expect` | object | See below |

## Expectations

Only the keys present are checked, so a vector asserts exactly what it means to.

| Key | Type | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `legal` | bool | Whether `move` is accepted |
| `reason` | string | Rejection code: `occupied`, `suicide`, `ko`, `superko`, `not_your_turn`, `out_of_bounds`, `game_not_playing` |
| `captured` | [coordinate] | Stones removed by `move` |
| `captures_after` | `{black, white}` | Prisoner counts once `move` is applied |
| `ko_point` | coordinate | The ko point `move` creates |
| `ko_point_absent` | bool | Asserts no ko point was created |
| `phase` | `playing` \| `scoring` \| `finished` | Phase after `move` |
| `result` | `{winner, reason}` | Game result; `winner` may be `null` for a void game |
| `territory` | `{black, white}` | Surrounded points after removing dead stones |
| `neutral` | int | Points bordered by both colours (dame) |
| `area` | `{black, white}` | Chinese area counts |
| `score` | `{black, white}` | Final totals including komi |
| `winner` / `margin` | string / number | Derived from `score` |
| `pass_alive` | `{black: [], white: []}` | Benson's unconditionally-alive stones |
| `handicap_stones` | [coordinate] | Where handicap stones land |
| `to_play` / `komi` / `move_number` | | Starting state for handicap vectors |
| `history_contains_start` | bool | The starting position must be in the superko history |
| `history_size` | int | Number of distinct positions recorded |
| `sgf_contains` | [string] | Substrings the encoded SGF must contain |
| `round_trip` | bool | Encode then decode must preserve the record |

## Current coverage

| Group | Vectors | Target ([09 §3.3](../docs/09-testing-strategy.md)) |
|---|---|---|
| `legality` | 9 | 60 |
| `capture` | 5 | 80 |
| `suicide` | 4 | 40 |
| `ko` | 5 | 50 |
| `superko` | 2 | 30 |
| `life_death` | 3 | 60 |
| `scoring` | 4 | 70 |
| `handicap` | 8 | 30 |
| `sgf` | 3 | 20 |
| **Total** | **43** | **440** |

The gap is deliberate: these 43 are the cases that can be verified by hand from
the specification. The remainder are meant to come from the two sources the
strategy document already names — the SGF corpus and the nightly differential
run — neither of which is wired up yet.

### Known gap: long repetition cycles

`superko/` covers positional superko only where it is reachable in two moves (a
basic ko under Chinese rules). Triple ko and *sending two returning one* need
roughly a dozen stones placed exactly, and cannot be verified by hand with any
confidence. Until the differential runner exists, these paths are covered by
code inspection alone. The same gap applies to Japanese repetition
([02 §4.3](../docs/02-go-rules-spec.md#43-lặp-thế-trong-hệ-luật-nhật-triple-ko)):
under Japanese rules basic ko blocks the two-move repeat, so the void-game path
never triggers in any vector here.

## Adding a vector

1. Write the expectation from the specification, by hand.
2. Add it to `tools/gen_vectors.py` and run it.
3. Run both suites. If an engine disagrees, decide which is wrong before touching either.
4. A behaviour change means a new `rules_version` in `VERSION`.
